lesson.mp.invite.title: Send the invite
lesson.mp.invite.body: Jay copies the invite when the room opens. Send it to your friend in a private chat. It only works while your room is open.
lesson.mp.knock.title: Check the safety code when a friend knocks
lesson.mp.knock.body: Your friend reads out the code on their screen. Let them in only if it is exactly the same as the one Jay shows you.
lesson.mp.lan.title: Open your world to LAN first
lesson.mp.lan.body: In Minecraft, enter your world, press Esc and select “Open to LAN”. Jay finds the game by itself. Friends who join don't need this step.
lesson.mp.trouble.title: If it won't connect
lesson.mp.trouble.body: Open “Connection problems?” at the bottom of the page. One check tells you what is going on and what to try next.
lesson.safe.invite.title: Only send invites to people you know
lesson.safe.invite.body: Anyone with your invite can knock. Send it in a private chat, never in a public group or a video.
lesson.safe.codes.title: Same safety code, then let in
lesson.safe.codes.body: If even one character is different, don't let them in. Ask your friend to knock again.
lesson.safe.remote.title: Remote help is only for people you trust
lesson.safe.remote.body: It hands over your mouse and keyboard. Nobody from Jay will ever ask you for it.
lesson.safe.program.title: Don't open program files from others
lesson.safe.program.body: Files like .exe, .bat or .jar can run on your computer. Jay warns you when someone sends one.
lesson.safe.public.title: What others see in public rooms
lesson.safe.public.body: The public list shows the room name, the host's player name, the game version and how many people are in. Only open a room to the public when you are happy for strangers to knock.

home.sandbox.consent.title: Strong sandbox for the game
home.sandbox.consent.body:
Jay runs the game in a Windows AppContainer, so it cannot see Jay's data, your browsers or your other files. Windows needs one admin confirmation, once, for two things: letting the game talk to Jay on this computer (loopback, for multiplayer), and letting sandboxed apps see the names in the folders above the game folder (only names, only those folders, nothing inside them), which Java needs to find its files.

If you say no, the game uses the standard sandbox and Jay will not ask again. You can retry, or remove these permissions again, in Settings › Privacy & security.

settings.sandbox.strong.hint: Windows: the game runs in an AppContainer and sees only its own folders, not Jay's data or your browsers. people.empty.body: Send a friend your friend code, or paste theirs. The two of you compare four emoji once; after that you invite each other without passing codes around.

multiplayer.open.who.invited_detail: Only the people you send an invite to can come. Nobody else can find the room.
multiplayer.open.who.friends_detail: Your friends are told the room is open and can knock without an invite. You still say yes to each one.
multiplayer.open.who.public_detail: Listed on the connected network, where anyone can find it. With a password, only people who know it get in.
multiplayer.open.route.auto_detail: Direct when it works, through relays when it doesn't. Usually the fastest. People in the room can see each other's IP address.
multiplayer.open.route.relay_detail: Everything goes through relays, so people in the room don't see each other's IP address. A little slower.
multiplayer.open.route.serverless_detail: No relay and no network: the two computers connect straight to each other and never fall back to a relay. You get a code with your address encrypted by a passphrase, for one friend at a time. To find that address, Jay asks the STUN servers listed in multiplayer settings, and they see your IP address.
multiplayer.open.route.serverless_note: The button makes a code and a passphrase. Send the code, and tell the passphrase another way (a call, in person). The code works once, for 10 minutes.
multiplayer.open.protection.standard_det: Each member gets their own encrypted channel. Right for almost everyone.
multiplayer.open.protection.stronger_det: Also changes keys every 10 minutes and evens out packet sizes, so sizes give less away.
multiplayer.open.protection.highest_deta: Changes keys every minute, pads every packet to one size, adds cover traffic and makes the connection look like a Minecraft login. Uses much more data.
multiplayer.open.scope.game_detail: Only the game you opened is shared. Nothing else on your computer can be reached.
multiplayer.open.scope.lan_detail: A virtual LAN for every program, like being on the same Wi-Fi. Needs administrator rights.

multiplayer.open.blocked.serverless: This needs a network, so it can't be used with “No server”.
